question: Agar consideration unlawful ho to kya contract void hai?
short_answer: Ji haan, agar kisi muahiday (agreement) ka maqsad ya consideration ghair qanooni (unlawful) ho, to woh muahida void hota hai.
explanation: Contract Act, 1872 ke mutabiq, har woh muahida jiska maqsad ya consideration ghair qanooni ho, void qarar diya jata hai. Mazeed bar-aan, agar consideration ka koi hissa bhi ghair qanooni ho, to poora muahida void ho jata hai.

citations.title: What considerations and objects are lawful and what not
citations.quote: Every agreement of which the object or consideration is unlawful is void.

citations.title: Agreements void, if considerations and objects unlawful in part
citations.quote: If any part of a single consideration for one or more objects, or anyone or any part of anyone of several considerations for a single object, is unlawful, the agreement is void.

retrieved.source: Lahore High Court | Writ Petition No.12069 of 2010 | para 22 | page 28

question: What is the punishment for qatl-e-amd under the Pakistan Penal Code?
short_answer: The punishment for qatl-e-amd includes death as qisas, death or life imprisonment as ta'zir, or imprisonment for up to twenty-five years depending on the circumstances and availability of proof.
explanation: Under Section 302 of the Pakistan Penal Code, qatl-e-amd is punishable by death as qisas, death or life imprisonment as ta'zir if specific proof is unavailable, or imprisonment up to twenty-five years where qisas is not applicable, subject to the proviso regarding fasad-fil-arz.

citations.title: Punishment of qatl-e-amd
citations.quote: Whoever commits qatl-e-amd shall, subject to the provisions of this Chapter be __ (a) punished with death as qisas; (b) punished with death for imprisonment for life as ta'zir having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, if the proof in either of the forms specified in section 304 is not available; or (c) punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to twenty- five years, where according to the Injunctions of Islam the punishment of qisas is not applicable.

question: What did the Supreme Court say about the duty of police when a court dismisses a pre-arrest bail application?
short_answer: When a court dismisses a pre-arrest bail application, police authorities are legally bound to implement the order immediately and execute the arrest without delay.
explanation: The Supreme Court has clarified that the dismissal of pre-arrest bail means the accused is subject to lawful arrest. Police must not treat the mere filing of a petition in a higher court as an implied stay of arrest; they must act promptly and in good faith unless an express restraining order is granted by a competent court.

citations.act_or_case: Zahid Khan, etc v. The State through Prosecutor General, Punjab and another
citations.quote: Absent such an order, a refusal of bail remains fully operative and must be implemented promptly and in good faith by investigating authorities.

citations.act_or_case: Zahid Khan, etc v. The State through Prosecutor General, Punjab and another
citations.quote: This Court, therefore, finds it imperative to state clearly that investigating officers and police authorities are legally bound to act upon court orders dismissing pre-arrest bail immediately, without waiting for further instructions or presuming the existence of any stay where none has been granted.
